clue.text: In dining room English crazy about French ladies

indicators.note: the dining room's letters go around the rest, so the rest sits in it

parts.note: a mess is a dining room for service personnel

indicators.note: about signals turning the English abbreviation and the word for crazy round together

parts.note: crazy means mad

explanation.surface: A deranged Englishman in the officers' mess makes a fuss over some women from France.
explanation.walkthrough: A mess is the communal dining room of a military unit; 'about' turns round both the English letter and the word for crazy, not just the latter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesdames is the French plural form used to address several married women.

clue.text: Continents considered as a whole one in ruined US area

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed in the rearranged letters
ruined suggests the letters of US and area are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Talk of global landmasses meets a blighted patch of American land.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia is the single landmass formed by Europe and Asia taken together.

clue.text: Where conflict arises at sea, these charges may be dropped

definitions.text: Where conflict arises at sea, these charges may be dropped

parts.words: Where conflict arises at sea, these charges may be dropped
parts.note: the charges are explosives dropped from ships against submarines, not legal accusations being withdrawn

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like legal charges being dropped; really these are depth charges, explosives rolled off warships in naval combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth charges are anti-submarine bombs set to explode underwater at a chosen level.

clue.text: Locus for enthusiasts regularly using revolutionary toy

parts.note: a mecca is a place that draws devotees of something

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to be on a drug is to be taking it regularly

explanation.surface: A favourite haunt of hobbyists where a radical plaything is constantly in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly using' is not a letter-pick: being on a medicine means taking it regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Meccano is a British construction kit of metal strips, nuts and bolts for building models.

clue.text: Furious book by 6A 25

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the 2023 memoir by Prince Harry

explanation.walkthrough: 6A and 25 together give PRINCE HARRY, whose memoir was titled after his status as the 'spare' heir.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this word for livid, and it is also the title of the royal's autobiography.

clue.text: Musician in north cutting cost

indicators.note: the letter for north cuts into the word for cost, landing inside it

parts.note: cost means price

explanation.surface: A performer up north is slashing what he charges.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince was the American singer and multi-instrumentalist behind Purple Rain.

clue.text: Irritable character in 18 sent up having accepted six shillings

indicators.note: the reversed name takes in the other letters, which end up inside it
in a down clue, sent up means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Uriah Heep is a character in David Copperfield by Dickens (18)
VI is six in Roman numerals
S is the abbreviation for shillings, an old British coin

explanation.surface: A grumpy Dickens figure is mocked after pocketing a small bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is the scheming clerk of David Copperfield; 'sent up' suits a down entry, where reversing means reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone peevish is easily annoyed, fretful and bad-tempered.

clue.text: Similar in every detail, papers a client misplaced

parts.note: ID means identity papers

indicators.note: misplaced means the letters of a client are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A customer has lost some documents that matched exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical things are exact copies, alike in all respects.

clue.text: Rook with flatfish brings comfort when distressed

parts.note: to rook is to swindle, as is to con
a sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A chess piece and a fish somehow cheer up someone who is upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To console is to offer solace to someone grieving or upset.

clue.text: Purchase a raven 20 18 kept

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a firm hold, as in getting purchase on something
second meaning: the pet raven of Charles Dickens (20 18), model for the bird in Barnaby Rudge

explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like buying, but here it is a hold. 20 and 18 combine to name CHARLES DICKENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Grip is a firm hold, the sense of purchase as leverage, and the name of Dickens's pet bird.

clue.text: Fickle folk, English, tucking into fruit after tea

indicators.note: the fruit-based part follows the word for tea

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

indicators.note: the letter for English is tucked inside the fruit

parts.note: melons are fruit

explanation.surface: An Englishman eats fruit after his cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: Chameleons change colour, so the word is used for changeable, inconstant people.

clue.text: Condition in maths reworked attracting top grade

indicators.note: the rearranged letters draw the grade letter to their end
reworked suggests the letters of maths are redone in a new order

parts.note: A is the highest exam grade

explanation.surface: A medical issue arises in a redone maths paper that earns the best mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a chronic respiratory illness that narrows the airways.

clue.text: Compulsory turn-out?

parts.note: turn-out suggests attendance or a vote, but here it is being turned out of one's home by force

explanation.walkthrough: A compulsory turn-out sounds like mandatory voting; read 'turn out' as expel and it is a forced removal from a property.
explanation.definitionFit: An eviction is the legal expulsion of a tenant from premises.

clue.text: 6A's observation on excessive tabloid exposure?

parts.note: Hamlet, Prince of Denmark, puns on 'sun' and 'son'; here the Sun is also a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's retort to Claudius in Act 1 is reread as a royal complaining of over-coverage in The Sun, a British tabloid; 6A is PRINCE, as in Hamlet and Harry.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted line is spoken by Shakespeare's Danish royal, whose pun on son fits press intrusion.

clue.text: Give encouraging cry during ecstasy

indicators.note: the cry occurs during the ecstasy, so sits inside it

parts.note: a trance is a state of rapture or ecstasy
ole is the cheer of a bullfight crowd

explanation.surface: Cheer someone on while in a state of rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: the slack in a rope or a mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance as in allowable play or slack in engineering matches give, the capacity to yield.

clue.text: Muslims occasionally seen in German city

indicators.note: occasionally means only some letters count, every other one

explanation.surface: Followers of Islam are sometimes spotted in a city in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulm is a city on the Danube in Baden-Württemberg, Einstein's birthplace.

clue.text: Native American doctrine unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a creed is a doctrine or set of beliefs

explanation.surface: An Indigenous people's belief system remains incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cree are a First Nations people of Canada and the northern United States.

clue.text: Hero unemployed reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means what follows is as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: idle means out of work

explanation.surface: A celebrated figure is said to be out of a job.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is someone admired or worshipped, a hero figure.

clue.text: Elevated hero in Scotland knows devil

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means the word is raised, read upwards

parts.note: El Cid is the Spanish national hero
ken means know in Scottish usage

explanation.surface: A lofty champion in Scotland recognises Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: CID read upwards gives DIC, then KENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens is a euphemism for the devil, as in 'what the dickens'.

clue.text: Faultless conception of a particular religion?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: perfectly clean, without flaw
second meaning; the question mark marks the playful reading

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one phrase about perfect conception, but splits after 'Faultless'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means spotless, and in Catholic teaching names Mary's conception free of original sin.

clue.text: See 13
25's old man in check on French city

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
Arles is a city in Provence

explanation.surface: Harry's father keeps an eye on a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: King Charles III is the father of Prince Harry (25).

clue.text: With a will, the nation bans heroin

indicators.note: bans means the drug's letter is kept out of the words

parts.note: a state is a nation
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A determined country outlaws a hard drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a will' looks like 'determinedly', but it means having made a legal will.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone testate died having left a valid legal testament.

clue.text: In the 20s perhaps champion advances rapidly

indicators.note: the champion abbreviation goes in the twenties

parts.note: a score is twenty, so twenties are scores

explanation.surface: A sporting star of the Roaring Twenties races ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The 20s' hints at the decade, but it is plural twenties: scores.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch is informal for to travel at high speed, especially by car or bike.

clue.text: Part of flight with one 19D?

indicators.note: the star takes the letter for one with it, holding it inside

parts.note: the end of 19D, 'the sun', is a star
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Flying high alongside the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the sun is just one example of a star.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is made of single steps, each a stair.

clue.text: Gulag has thirty guards filled with terror

indicators.note: guards means the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A prison camp holds thirty terrified inmates.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast describes being struck with horror or shock.

clue.text: Badger would be dangerous with one coming in for a run

indicators.note: says one letter takes another's place; here it tells how the answer becomes the word for dangerous

parts.note: hairy is slang for dangerous
I is one in Roman numerals
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A burrowing animal would be risky if one rushed in.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: the answer would become HAIRY if I came in for R. So start from HAIRY and put R back for the I.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger and to harry both mean to pester or harass persistently.

clue.text: Finch, outside science rooms, backing participant in rally?

indicators.note: backing means the whole construction is read from right to left
the bird goes outside the rooms, holding them

parts.note: a linnet is a kind of finch
labs are science rooms

explanation.surface: A bird around the laboratories supports someone at a political rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' applies to the whole container, not just the finch. A rally here is a long tennis exchange, not a demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a rally is an exchange of shots, and the ball is part of every stroke.

clue.text: Use phone when abroad — ring to break strike?

indicators.note: the ring breaks into the word for strike, sitting inside

parts.note: to ram is to strike
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A call to someone overseas during an industrial walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests a walkout, but it means hit; 'ring' suggests a call, but it is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile users roam when their phone connects through foreign networks while travelling.

clue.text: Seat moved, by sailors, towards the rear

indicators.note: moved signals the letters of seat being shifted around

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Navy men shift a bench back toward the stern.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is nautical for behind the vessel or backwards.

clue.text: Grass surrounding lake after dump transformed

indicators.note: the grass word goes round the rest

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: the lake's letter follows the dump

parts.note: a sty is a filthy place, a dump
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Turf around a pond near the tip has been redone.
explanation.definitionFit: Restyled means given a new look or design, made over.
